references.authors: Abbas SM, Basalamah AH
references.title: Effects of Ramadhan fast on male fertility.
references.finding: Small study: Ramadan did not harm semen in healthy men; LH and semen volume fell after the fast while sperm count rose during it.

references.authors: Cameron JL, Weltzin TE, McConaha C, et al.
references.title: Slowing of pulsatile luteinizing hormone secretion in men after forty-eight hours of fasting.
references.finding: 48 h of fasting cut mean LH from 2.94 to 1.07 IU/L and halved LH pulse frequency, and lowered FSH and testosterone, without a rise in cortisol.

references.authors: Cienfuegos S, Corapi S, Gabel K, et al.
references.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Reproductive Hormone Levels in Females and Males: A Review of Human Trials.
references.finding: Review of human trials: IF lowers testosterone/free androgen index and raises SHBG in premenopausal women with obesity, does not change oestrogen or gonadotropins, and lowers testosterone in lean active young men.

references.authors: Engel OJ, Doctory N, Sun B, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Month-Long Daily Fasting on Semen Parameters: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
references.finding: Semen samples produced during Ramadan (and 70 days after) had lower post-gradient progressive motility (30% vs 38%) and lower volume than the same men's samples at other times (retrospective).

references.authors: May KT, Behling J, Sochiera-Plegniere K, et al.
references.title: Fasting for male fertility-a mixed methods study.
references.finding: Three 5-day 500 kcal FMD cycles over 4 months produced no clear differences in semen parameters vs waiting-list controls (pilot, underpowered).

references.authors: Moro T, Tinsley G, Bianco A, et al.
references.title: Effects of eight weeks of time-restricted feeding (16/8) on basal metabolism, maximal strength, body composition, inflammation, and cardiovascular risk factors in resistance-trained males.
references.finding: 8 weeks of isocaloric 16:8 TRE with resistance training reduced fat mass, preserved lean mass and strength, but lowered testosterone, IGF-1 and T3.

references.authors: Poursalehian M, Mohseni S, Shadman Z, et al.
references.title: Impact of Ramadan fasting on serum levels of major endocrinology hormonal and biochemical parameters in healthy non-athlete adults: A systematic review and meta-analyses.
references.finding: Ramadan fasting did not significantly change testosterone, LH, FSH, prolactin or thyroid hormones in healthy non-athletes; morning cortisol tended to fall.

references.authors: Aerts A, Temmerman A, Vanhie A, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Endurance Exercise on Semen Quality in Male Athletes: A Systematic Review.
references.finding: Endurance exercise can lower semen quality, but changes were usually not clinically relevant; some cyclists and triathletes had more abnormal morphology or DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Cupka M, Sedliak M
references.title: Hungry runners - low energy availability in male endurance athletes and its impact on performance and testosterone: mini-review.
references.finding: Low energy availability is common in male endurance athletes and correlates with lower testosterone, bone density and resting metabolic rate.

references.authors: De Souza MJ, Arce JC, Pescatello LS, et al.
references.title: Gonadal hormones and semen quality in male runners. A volume threshold effect of endurance training.
references.finding: High-mileage runners (~108 km/week) had lower testosterone, sperm motility and density than moderate-mileage runners or sedentary men.

references.authors: Hackney AC
references.title: Effects of endurance exercise on the reproductive system of men: the "exercise-hypogonadal male condition".
references.finding: Describes the exercise-hypogonadal male condition as limited to men with years of chronic endurance training and not highly prevalent.

references.authors: Hackney AC, Lane AR, Register-Mihalik J, et al.
references.title: Endurance Exercise Training and Male Sexual Libido.
references.finding: Men with the highest training intensity and duration had greater odds of low libido than those training least.

references.authors: Hackney AC
references.title: Hypogonadism in Exercising Males: Dysfunction or Adaptive-Regulatory Adjustment?
references.finding: Proposes several forms of exercise-related male hypogonadism, some transient and linked to low energy availability or overtraining, others possibly an adaptive readjustment.

references.authors: Ibañez-Perez J, Santos-Zorrozua B, Lopez-Lopez E, et al.
references.title: An update on the implication of physical activity on semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Most data show no major effect of activity on semen; recreational activity may help concentration or motility, while elite activity may harm motility, and cycling may lower concentration.

references.authors: Lane AR, Magallanes CA, Hackney AC
references.title: Reproductive Dysfunction from Exercise Training: The "Exercise-Hypogonadal Male Condition".
references.finding: Men chronically doing endurance training can show persistently low free and total testosterone without raised LH ('exercise-hypogonadal male condition'); spermatogenesis problems may occur in some.

references.authors: Mountjoy M, Ackerman KE, Bailey DM, et al.
references.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee's (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs).
references.finding: IOC 2023 consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), covering reproductive suppression from low energy availability in both sexes.

references.authors: Vaamonde D, Algar-Santacruz C, Abbasi A, et al.
references.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation as a result of ultra-endurance exercise training in male athletes.
references.finding: Elite triathletes in training had high sperm DNA fragmentation (mean 20.4%) and raised round cells.

references.authors: Wise LA, Cramer DW, Hornstein MD, et al.
references.title: Physical activity and semen quality among men attending an infertility clinic.
references.finding: Regular exercise was not associated with semen quality overall, but cycling 5+ h/week was linked to low sperm concentration (OR 1.92).

references.authors: Wise LA, Wang TR, Ulrichsen SP, et al.
references.title: A prospective study of male physical activity and fecundability.
references.finding: Male vigorous, moderate or total activity was not consistently associated with couples' fecundability.

references.authors: Agarwal A, Deepinder F, Cocuzza M, et al.
references.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on sperm motility and chromatin integrity: a prospective comparative study.
references.finding: In vitro, FemGlide, Replens and Astroglide reduced progressive motility and FemGlide and K-Y Jelly raised DNA fragmentation (SCSA), whereas Pre-Seed did not differ from culture medium.

references.authors: Agarwal A, Malvezzi H, Sharma R
references.title: Effect of an isotonic lubricant on sperm collection and sperm quality.
references.finding: Using Pre-Seed during masturbation for semen collection did not change motility, viability, ROS, antioxidant capacity or DNA damage.

references.authors: Anderson L, Lewis SE, McClure N
references.title: The effects of coital lubricants on sperm motility in vitro.
references.finding: K-Y jelly, olive oil and saliva (but not baby oil) significantly reduced sperm motility in vitro at 12.5%; olive oil and saliva still did at 6.25%.

references.authors: Bach CC, Vested A, Jørgensen KT, et al.
references.title: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances and measures of human fertility: a systematic review.
references.finding: Little consistent evidence that PFAS affect semen quality or hormones in men; associations with longer time to pregnancy appear in parous women and are most likely not causal.

references.authors: Di Nisio A, López-Gil JF, Pizzol D, et al.
references.title: Associations between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen parameters: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: PFAS were weakly associated with lower progressive motility (r = -0.058) and more sperm DNA fragmentation (r = 0.141), with little association with standard counts.

references.authors: Due I, Rubio L, Catalán J, et al.
references.title: Mammalian reproductive and developmental toxicity of micro- and nanoplastics: a critical appraisal of evidence using the SciRAP tool.
references.finding: Systematic appraisal of in vivo mammalian micro/nanoplastic reproductive studies: many report harm to testis, ovary and gametes, but particle characterization, dose and dose-response were often missing.

references.authors: Gumerova E, Rimmer MP, Gellatly SA
references.title: Do sperm and lubricants gel well with each other? A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review: only 2 of 24 studies were in vivo; methodological variation and absent pregnancy outcomes prevent an evidence-based "sperm-safe" lubricant guideline.

references.authors: Guo Y, Rong M, Fan Y, et al.
references.title: The Presence of Microplastics in Human Semen and Their Associations with Semen Quality.
references.finding: Laser-direct infrared found microplastics in 34 of 45 semen samples; men with PET particles had borderline lower progressive motility (20.6% vs 34.9%, p=0.056) and no difference in concentration or count.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis.
references.finding: Pyrolysis-GC/MS reported microplastics in every testis (mean 328 ug/g in humans, 123 ug/g in dogs), mostly polyethylene; in dogs PVC and PET levels correlated with lower normalized testis weight.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Response to comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
references.finding: Authors' reply: controls were described in their placenta paper; after re-evaluation only 6 of the 12 polymers (PE, PP, PVC, nylon, SBR, PET) give enough confidence for health-based work.

references.authors: Joensen UN, Bossi R, Leffers H, et al.
references.title: Do perfluoroalkyl compounds impair human semen quality?
references.finding: Men with high combined PFOS+PFOA had fewer morphologically normal sperm (6.2 vs 15.5 million per ejaculate).

references.authors: Li N, Yang H, Dong Y, et al.
references.title: Prevalence and implications of microplastic contaminants in general human seminal fluid: A Raman spectroscopic study.
references.finding: Raman found about 2 microplastic particles per semen sample in all 40 men (mostly polystyrene); PVC-containing samples had lower progressive motility than polystyrene-containing ones.

references.authors: Louis GM, Chen Z, Schisterman EF, et al.
references.title: Perfluorochemicals and human semen quality: the LIFE study.
references.finding: Several PFAS were associated with some semen endpoints, but in varying directions; strongest signals were for PFOSA and sperm head morphology.

references.authors: Mackenzie SC, Gellatly SA
references.title: Vaginal lubricants in the couple trying-to-conceive: Assessing healthcare professional recommendations and effect on in vitro sperm function.
references.n: 32 clinician survey responses plus lab testing
references.finding: Aquagel cut progressive motility to 49% of control within 10 min even at 5%, while a sperm-safe lubricant (Pre) had no effect; clinicians' advice was inconsistent.

references.authors: McInerney KA, Hahn KA, Hatch EE, et al.
references.title: Lubricant use during intercourse and time to pregnancy: a prospective cohort study.
references.finding: No lubricant type was associated with lower fecundability (water-based FR 1.02; "fertility-friendly" 1.01; oil-based 1.23; silicone 1.27).

references.authors: Mesen TB, Steiner AZ
references.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
references.finding: In vitro, many lubricants are sperm-toxic while "sperm-friendly" ones are not, yet cohort data show no effect on fecundity; an RCT is needed.

references.authors: Montano L, Giorgini E, Notarstefano V, et al.
references.title: Raman Microspectroscopy evidence of microplastics in human semen.
references.finding: Raman microspectroscopy found 16 microplastic fragments (2-6 um) in 6 of 10 semen samples from a polluted area of southern Italy.

references.authors: Mowat A, Newton C, Boothroyd C, et al.
references.title: The effects of vaginal lubricants on sperm function: an in vitro analysis.
references.finding: Of nine lubricants tested in vitro, Pre-Seed preserved motility (86%) and vitality (92%) best and Conceive Plus was second; none affected DNA fragmentation over 30 min.

references.authors: Rauert C, Charlton N, Bagley A, et al.
references.title: Assessing the Efficacy of Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for Nanoplastic and Microplastic Analysis in Human Blood.
references.finding: Validation study concluding that Py-GC/MS is currently not suitable for polyethylene and PVC in biological matrices because of interferences, with realistic detection limits up to 20x higher than nominal and no other polymers detectable in human blood.

references.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
references.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
references.finding: Parabens at concentrations found in vaginal lubricants generated mitochondrial ROS and oxidative DNA adducts and reduced sperm motility and viability in vitro.

references.authors: Specht IO, Hougaard KS, Spanò M, et al.
references.title: Sperm DNA integrity in relation to exposure to environmental perfluoroalkyl substances - a study of spouses of pregnant women in three geographical regions.
references.finding: No consistent association between serum PFAS and sperm DNA fragmentation (SCSA), apoptosis markers or reproductive hormones; only a slight TUNEL rise with PFOA in Greenland.

references.authors: Steiner AZ, Long DL, Tanner C, et al.
references.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
references.finding: Lubricant use in the fertile window did not reduce fecundability (fecundability ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.59-1.85).

references.authors: Tomlinson J, Pooley K, Tomlinson M
references.title: Sperm toxicity testing on lubricant gels: should we be recommending 'fertility-friendly' specialist products?
references.finding: All gels reduced motility in vitro; products marketed as sperm-friendly (FertilSafe Plus) performed best, pleasure lubricants worst, and saliva was worse still.

references.authors: Tulandi T, Plouffe L, McInnes RA
references.title: Effect of saliva on sperm motility and activity.
references.finding: Saliva reduced sperm motility and progression in vitro, even at low concentrations.

references.authors: Uppu RM, Peijnenburg W, Hays SM
references.title: Comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
references.finding: Comment on Hu 2024: no reported blanks, negative/positive or background controls, unvalidated digestion and ultracentrifugation steps, and no LOD/LOQ, internal standards or matrix spikes for the Py-GC/MS method.

references.authors: Wang H, Wei K, Wu Z, et al.
references.title: Association between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen quality.
references.finding: PFOA and PFNA were associated with lower progressive sperm motility; other semen parameters were largely unaffected.

references.authors: Zhao Q, Zhu L, Weng J, et al.
references.title: Detection and characterization of microplastics in the human testis and semen.
references.finding: Py-GC/MS and laser-direct infrared found microplastics in testis (11.6 particles/g) and semen (0.23 particles/mL), mostly 20-100 um.

references.authors: Akasheh G, Sirati L, Noshad Kamran AR, et al.
references.title: Comparison of the effect of sertraline with behavioral therapy on semen parameters in men with primary premature ejaculation.
references.finding: Sertraline 50 mg/day for 3 months (vs behavioural therapy) lowered sperm concentration and normal morphology and raised sperm DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Amory JK, Wang C, Swerdloff RS, et al.
references.title: The effect of 5alpha-reductase inhibition with dutasteride and finasteride on semen parameters and serum hormones in healthy men.
references.finding: Dutasteride 0.5 mg and finasteride 5 mg cut total sperm count by 28.6% and 34.3% at 26 weeks, lowered volume and motility, with largely reversible effects after stopping.

references.authors: Banerjee A, Scarpa M, Pathak S, et al.
references.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Therapies Adversely Affect Fertility in Men- A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
references.journal: Endocr Metab Immune Disord Drug Targets
references.finding: Sulphasalazine-treated men had lower sperm counts and motility and more oligospermia than mesalazine-treated men; biologics appeared safe.

references.authors: Bawor M, Bami H, Dennis BB, et al.
references.title: Testosterone suppression in opioid users: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Regular opioid use (including methadone) lowered testosterone in men by about 165 ng/dL versus controls; no effect seen in women.

references.authors: Beeder LA, Samplaski MK
references.title: Effect of antidepressant medications on semen parameters and male fertility.
references.finding: SSRIs, especially fluoxetine, are linked to lower sperm concentration and motility and higher DNA fragmentation in human and animal studies; effects appear reversible; data on other antidepressants are sparse.

references.authors: Drobnis EZ, Nangia AK
references.title: Pain Medications and Male Reproduction.
references.finding: Exogenous opioids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and act directly on the testis, lowering semen quality and raising DNA fragmentation; NSAIDs have less effect; paracetamol may be of concern.

references.authors: Eck LK, Jensen TB, Mastrogiannis D, et al.
references.title: Risk of Adverse Pregnancy Outcome After Paternal Exposure to Methotrexate Within 90 Days Before Pregnancy.
references.finding: Paternal methotrexate within 90 days before conception was not associated with major malformations (aOR 1.01), stillbirth or preterm birth.

references.authors: Evans-Hoeker EA, Eisenberg E, Diamond MP, et al.
references.title: Major depression, antidepressant use, and male and female fertility.
references.n: 1650 women and 1608 men in infertility trials
references.finding: Active major depression in the male partner lowered conception; maternal antidepressant use (n=90) was associated with first-trimester pregnancy loss.

references.authors: Gregorič N, Šikonja J, Janež A, et al.
references.title: Semaglutide improved sperm morphology in obese men with type 2 diabetes mellitus and functional hypogonadism.
references.n: obese men with type 2 diabetes and functional hypogonadism
references.finding: Semaglutide raised normal sperm morphology (median 2% to 4%) and testosterone, whereas testosterone therapy lowered sperm concentration and count.

references.authors: Hellstrom WJ, Sikka SC
references.title: Effects of acute treatment with tamsulosin versus alfuzosin on ejaculatory function in normal volunteers.
references.finding: Tamsulosin 0.8 mg daily lowered ejaculate volume by 2.4 mL and caused anejaculation in 35% of men; alfuzosin and placebo did not.

references.authors: Koyuncu H, Serefoglu EC, Yencilek E, et al.
references.title: Escitalopram treatment for premature ejaculation has a negative effect on semen parameters.
references.finding: Escitalopram 10 mg daily for 12 weeks lowered sperm concentration, motility and morphology.

references.authors: O'Moráin C, Smethurst P, Doré CJ, et al.
references.title: Reversible male infertility due to sulphasalazine: studies in man and rat.
references.n: men with IBD plus rat studies
references.finding: Sulphasalazine caused oligospermia, poor motility and abnormal forms that reversed on withdrawal (15 pregnancies at a median 2.5 months); the sulphapyridine moiety was responsible in rats.

references.authors: Overstreet JW, Fuh VL, Gould J, et al.
references.title: Chronic treatment with finasteride daily does not affect spermatogenesis or semen production in young men.
references.finding: Finasteride 1 mg daily for 48 weeks did not affect sperm concentration, count, motility or morphology versus placebo.

references.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Dolhain RJEM, Vorstenbosch S, et al.
references.title: The effect of paternal exposure to immunosuppressive drugs on sexual function, reproductive hormones, fertility, pregnancy and offspring outcomes: a systematic review.
references.finding: Clear negative effects on sperm for sulfasalazine and cyclophosphamide; dubious effects for methotrexate, colchicine and sirolimus; no large negative offspring effects of paternal immunosuppressants reported.

references.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Röder E, Krijthe BP, et al.
references.title: Is methotrexate safe for men with an immune-mediated inflammatory disease and an active desire to become a father? Results of a prospective cohort study (iFAME-MTX).
references.finding: Semen parameters and sperm DNA fragmentation did not change after starting low-dose methotrexate and matched healthy controls; methotrexate barely accumulated in sperm.

references.authors: Safarinejad MR
references.title: Sperm DNA damage and semen quality impairment after treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors detected using semen analysis and sperm chromatin structure assay.
references.finding: Reported lower sperm count and motility and higher DNA denaturation with SSRIs; the journal issued an Expression of Concern in 2023, so this paper should not be relied on.

references.authors: Sakata K, Morita T
references.title: Investigation of ejaculatory disorder by silodosin in the treatment of prostatic hyperplasia.
references.finding: Among sexually active men on silodosin, 95% reported ejaculatory disorder.

references.authors: Samplaski MK, Lo K, Grober E, et al.
references.title: Finasteride use in the male infertility population: effects on semen and hormone parameters.
references.finding: In men presenting with infertility while on finasteride (mean 1 mg/day), sperm counts rose on average 11.6-fold after stopping; 57% of severely oligospermic men rose above 15 million/mL.

references.authors: Sylvester C, Menke M, Gopalan P
references.title: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors and Fertility: Considerations for Couples Trying to Conceive.
references.finding: Insufficient evidence that SSRIs reduce female fertility or IVF outcomes; six of seven mostly poor-quality male studies found adverse effects on semen.

references.authors: Tanrikut C, Feldman AS, Altemus M, et al.
references.title: Adverse effect of paroxetine on sperm.
references.finding: Five weeks of paroxetine raised mean sperm DNA fragmentation from 13.8% to 30.3% (TUNEL); abnormal fragmentation rose from 9.7% to 50% of men (OR 9.3) without changes in standard semen parameters.

references.authors: Toovey S, Hudson E, Hendry WF, et al.
references.title: Sulphasalazine and male infertility: reversibility and possible mechanism.
references.finding: Sulphasalazine 2-4 g/day caused gross semen abnormalities in 18 men treated over 2 months; quality recovered after withdrawal and 10 pregnancies followed.

references.authors: Yland JJ, McKinnon CJ, Hatch EE, et al.
references.title: A Prospective Study of Male Depression, Psychotropic Medication Use, and Fecundability.
references.finding: Male depression history was weakly associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.89, CI crossing 1); current psychotropic medication use statistically mediated 44% of the depressive-symptom association.

references.authors: Practice Committees of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
references.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) for non-male factor indications: a committee opinion
references.finding: ASRM/SART committee opinion reviewing when ICSI may or may not benefit couples whose semen meets WHO reference values; routine ICSI for non-male factor is not supported.

references.authors: Aydın Ş, Bulgan Kılıçdağ E, Çağlar Aytaç P, et al.
references.title: Prospective randomized controlled study of a microfluidic chip technology for sperm selection in male infertility patients
references.finding: Single-centre RCT in male-factor ICSI: microfluidic chip vs swim-up gave similar fertilisation and embryo quality but higher live birth (46.8% vs 25%).

references.authors: Boulet SL, Mehta A, Kissin DM, et al.
references.title: Trends in use of and reproductive outcomes associated with intracytoplasmic sperm injection
references.finding: US registry: ICSI use without male factor rose from 15.4% to 66.9% (1996-2012) and, in those cycles, was associated with slightly lower live birth than conventional IVF (36.5% vs 39.2%; aRR 0.95).

references.authors: Dang VQ, Vuong LN, Luu TM, et al.
references.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection versus conventional in-vitro fertilisation in couples with infertility in whom the male partner has normal total sperm count and motility: an open-label, randomised controlled trial
references.finding: In couples with normal sperm count and motility, ICSI did not raise live birth over conventional IVF (35% vs 31%; RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.93-1.32); total fertilisation failure was similar (5% vs 6%).

references.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, Bozdag G, et al.
references.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine
references.finding: ESHRE good practice recommendations on 42 add-ons: none based on high-quality evidence; not recommended include endometrial receptivity tests, immune testing and immunomodulators (Intralipid, IVIG), glucocorticoids, assisted hatching, time-lapse imaging (to improve live birth), intrauterine hCG, intrauterine and intraovarian PRP, mitochondrial replacement, adjuncts during stimulation (growth hormone, DHEA, testosterone), oral antioxidants and ICSI for non-male factor; PGT-A, endometrial scratching, MACS, PICSI and IMSI 'not recommended for routine clinical use'; microfluidics 'can be considered'; hyaluronan in transfer medium 'recommended' (with single embryo transfer).

references.authors: Garg A, Nakhla O, Steeper M, et al.
references.title: Advanced sperm selection techniques for assisted reproduction
references.finding: Cochrane 2026: hyaluronan-selected ICSI may make no or a slight difference to live birth (RR 1.09, 0.97-1.24; low certainty) and probably slightly reduces miscarriage (RR 0.59; moderate); effects of other techniques (MACS, microfluidics, IMSI) unknown due to very low certainty.

references.authors: Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA)
references.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
references.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

references.authors: Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA)
references.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation: treatment add-on rating
references.finding: After SDF testing: antioxidants and sperm selection (DGC/MACS with ICSI or PICSI) rated grey (insufficient evidence) for male factor and recurrent pregnancy loss; testicular sperm (TESE/TESA) with ICSI rated red for male factor (insufficient evidence plus surgical risk). Reviewed 24 Sep 2026.

references.authors: Huong DT, Tam DTM, Hoa NT, et al.
references.title: Comparative Efficacy of Microfluidics and Density Gradient Centrifugation for Sperm Preparation in IVF: A Randomized Controlled Trial
references.finding: Microfluidic preparation lowered sperm DNA fragmentation index more than density gradients, especially with high baseline DFI, but did not improve pregnancy or live birth.

references.authors: Mantravadi KC, Rao D
references.title: In cases with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, can sperm selection by magnetic-activated cell sorting or testicular sperm aspiration help improve reproductive outcomes?
references.n: couples with failed IVF and SDF >30%
references.finding: In couples with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, MACS-selected and testicular sperm gave comparable live birth; no control arm without either.

references.authors: Miller D, Pavitt S, Sharma V, et al.
references.title: Physiological, hyaluronan-selected intracytoplasmic sperm injection for infertility treatment (HABSelect): a parallel, two-group, randomised trial
references.finding: HABSelect: hyaluronan-selected sperm (PICSI) did not raise term live birth vs ICSI (27.4% vs 25.2%; OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.95-1.34); miscarriage was a secondary finding.

references.authors: Romany L, Garrido N, Motato Y, et al.
references.title: Removal of annexin V-positive sperm cells for intracytoplasmic sperm injection in ovum donation cycles does not improve reproductive outcome: a controlled and randomized trial in unselected males
references.finding: Removing annexin V-positive sperm by MACS did not improve fertilisation, embryo quality or live birth (48.4% vs 56.4%, NS) in donor-egg ICSI.

references.authors: Ammar O, Houas Z, Mehdi M
references.title: The association between iron, calcium, and oxidative stress in seminal plasma and sperm quality
references.finding: Seminal iron was higher in subfertile men and correlated negatively with sperm motility and normal morphology.

references.authors: Carlomagno F, Tenuta M, Sansone A, et al.
references.title: Iron overload disorders in adults: a comprehensive review of gonadal function, reproductive, and sexual health
references.n: Systematic review: 1201 men, 2134 women with iron overload
references.finding: In iron overload disorders, 47% of men had hypogonadism and over half of those assessed had azoospermia or other sperm abnormalities; early chelation helps prevent but rarely reverses damage.

references.authors: Dixon SJ, Lemberg KM, Lamprecht MR, et al.
references.title: Ferroptosis: an iron-dependent form of nonapoptotic cell death
references.finding: Defined ferroptosis: an iron-dependent, lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death triggered by cystine/glutathione depletion and blocked by ferrostatin-1.

references.authors: Perera D, Pizzey A, Campbell A, et al.
references.title: Sperm DNA damage in potentially fertile homozygous beta-thalassaemia patients with iron overload
references.finding: Iron-overloaded men (median ferritin 2251 ug/L) had more sperm DNA damage, which rose with later onset of chelation.

references.authors: Pilling LC, Tamosauskaite J, Jones G, et al.
references.title: Common conditions associated with hereditary haemochromatosis genetic variants: cohort study in UK Biobank
references.finding: HFE C282Y homozygosity (1 in 156) was associated with liver disease, arthritis and diabetes; diagnosed haemochromatosis in 21.7% of homozygous men and 9.8% of women.

references.authors: Abdelouahab N, Ainmelk Y, Takser L
references.title: Polybrominated diphenyl ethers and sperm quality.
references.finding: Serum BDE-47, BDE-100 and summed PBDEs were negatively related to sperm motility and thyroxine, with no relation to other semen parameters.

references.authors: Albert O, Huang JY, Aleksa K, et al.
references.title: Exposure to polybrominated diphenyl ethers and phthalates in healthy men living in the greater Montreal area: A study of hormonal balance and semen quality.
references.finding: Each 10-fold rise in BDE-47 was associated with borderline lower sperm concentration (-19.7%) and motility (-25.5%) but not with sperm chromatin damage (HT-COMET).

references.authors: Carignan CC, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Paternal urinary concentrations of organophosphate flame retardant metabolites, fertility measures, and pregnancy outcomes among couples undergoing in vitro fertilization.
references.finding: Paternal urinary OPFR metabolites were linked to a 12% lower fertilization proportion (2nd vs 1st quartile) and fewer best-quality embryos, but not consistently to implantation, pregnancy or live birth after adjusting for the female partner.

references.authors: Cherry N, Labrèche F, Collins J, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to solvents and male infertility.
references.finding: High solvent exposure was associated with motile sperm <12 million/mL (OR 3.83 in Montreal, 2.90 in a replication series); moderate exposure replicated in only one series.

references.authors: Cherry N, Moore H, McNamee R, et al.
references.title: Occupation and male infertility: glycol ethers and other exposures.
references.finding: High glycol ether exposure in the 3 months before the clinic visit was associated with low motile sperm count (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.08-4.69); moderate exposure OR 1.46 (0.93-2.28).

references.authors: Gibson EA, Stapleton HM, Calero L, et al.
references.title: Flame retardant exposure assessment: findings from a behavioral intervention study.
references.finding: One week of instructed house cleaning or hand-washing (then both) lowered some urinary flame-retardant metabolites and, in women with above-median baseline exposure, some hand-wipe levels, by about half in some cases.

references.authors: Ingle ME, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Carignan CC, et al.
references.title: The association between urinary concentrations of phosphorous-containing flame retardant metabolites and semen parameters among men from a fertility clinic.
references.finding: Associations between urinary OPFR metabolites and semen parameters were weak and inconsistent; BDCIPP was about 2-fold higher in summer samples.

references.authors: Li Y, Luo D, Zhao X, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of organophosphate esters in relation to semen quality: A cross-sectional study.
references.finding: Higher urinary DPHP and BMPP were associated with below-reference sperm count and OPE mixtures with lower motility and normal morphology.

references.authors: Lv MQ, Wang HX, Yang YQ, et al.
references.title: Semen Quality Following Long-term Occupational Exposure to Formaldehyde in China.
references.finding: Long-term occupational formaldehyde exposure index was associated with lower total and progressive sperm motility and velocity.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Stapleton HM
references.title: House dust concentrations of organophosphate flame retardants in relation to hormone levels and semen quality parameters.
references.finding: An interquartile rise in house-dust TPHP was associated with 19% lower sperm concentration and 10% higher prolactin; TDCPP with 3% lower free T4 and 17% higher prolactin.

references.authors: Moro AM, Charão M, Brucker N, et al.
references.title: Effects of low-level exposure to xenobiotics present in paints on oxidative stress in workers.
references.finding: Painters with solvent biomarkers below exposure limits had higher MDA and antioxidant enzyme activities and lower thiols and ALA-D than unexposed controls.

references.authors: Siddique S, Farhat I, Kubwabo C, et al.
references.title: Exposure of men living in the greater Montreal area to organophosphate esters: Association with hormonal balance and semen quality.
references.finding: Urinary OPE metabolites were nearly universally detected; a few were associated with hormone changes (e.g. TCIPP with lower testosterone) and some semen parameters.

references.authors: Snijder CA, te Velde E, Roeleveld N, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to chemical substances and time to pregnancy: a systematic review.
references.finding: Occupational lead and pesticides showed strong indications of longer time to pregnancy; evidence for organic solvents and other metals was equivocal.

references.authors: Tang W, Liu X, Cao Y, et al.
references.title: Exposure to individual organophosphate esters and their mixture in relation to semen quality in Chinese men.
references.finding: An organophosphate ester mixture was associated with lower progressive motility, but the signal was driven by organophosphate pesticide metabolites (DMTP), not flame-retardant metabolites.

references.authors: Wang HX, Li HC, Lv MQ, et al.
references.title: Associations between occupation exposure to Formaldehyde and semen quality, a primary study.
references.finding: Occupational formaldehyde exposure was associated with lower total and progressive sperm motility, with higher odds of abnormal motility at low and high exposure.

references.authors: Welch LS, Schrader SM, Turner TW, et al.
references.title: Effects of exposure to ethylene glycol ethers on shipyard painters: II. Male reproduction.
references.finding: Shipyard painters exposed to 2-ethoxyethanol and 2-methoxyethanol had more oligospermia and azoospermia and lower sperm counts.

references.authors: Yu YJ, Lin BG, Liang WB, et al.
references.title: Associations between PBDEs exposure from house dust and human semen quality at an e-waste areas in South China-A pilot study.
references.finding: Dust and semen PBDE levels correlated, and BDE-47/BDE-100 were negatively associated with sperm concentration, count and motility in an e-waste area.

references.authors: Adegbola CA, Akhigbe TM, Adeogun AE, et al.
references.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the impact of triclosan exposure on human semen quality.
references.finding: Pooled triclosan exposure was associated with lower sperm concentration (SMD -0.42) and total motility (SMD -1.30), with high heterogeneity.

references.authors: Adoamnei E, Mendiola J, Moñino-García M, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultra violet light filters and reproductive parameters in young men.
references.finding: Urinary BP-1 and BP-3 were weakly associated with higher FSH, but no BP-type filter was associated with any semen parameter; effects judged small and of unclear significance.

references.authors: Buck Louis GM, Kannan K, Sapra KJ, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultraviolet radiation filters and couples' fecundity.
references.finding: Men's urinary BP-2 (FOR 0.69) and 4-hydroxybenzophenone (FOR 0.74) were associated with lower couple fecundability; women's concentrations were not.

references.authors: Buck Louis GM, Chen Z, Kim S, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultraviolet light filters and semen quality.
references.finding: Among 35 semen endpoints, BP-2 was associated with lower concentration and some motility measures and BP-8 with two others; BP-1, BP-3 and 4OH-BP were not associated.

references.authors: Dodge LE, Williams PL, Williams MA, et al.
references.title: Paternal Urinary Concentrations of Parabens and Other Phenols in Relation to Reproductive Outcomes among Couples from a Fertility Clinic.
references.finding: Paternal urinary parabens and phenols were not associated with fertilization or live birth after IVF; an isolated second-quartile methylparaben association with lower IUI live birth lacked a dose-response.

references.authors: Hipwell AE, Kahn LG, Factor-Litvak P, et al.
references.title: Exposure to non-persistent chemicals in consumer products and fecundability: a systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review: preliminary support for female paraben and glycol ether exposure and male benzophenone exposure with longer time to pregnancy; little to no indication for BPA, triclosan or triclocarban; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

references.authors: Jaskulak M, Cinkusz M, Franchuk K, et al.
references.title: Endocrine and Reproductive Health Considerations of Sunscreen UV Filters: Insights from a Comprehensive Review 2014-2024.
references.finding: Review of 2014-2024 human evidence: benzophenones associated with poorer sperm quality in some studies, weaker findings for ovarian reserve, mixed prenatal results; stresses balancing endocrine concerns with photoprotection.

references.authors: Joensen UN, Jørgensen N, Thyssen JP, et al.
references.title: Urinary excretion of phenols, parabens and benzophenones in young men: Associations to reproductive hormones and semen quality are modified by mutations in the Filaggrin gene.
references.finding: Associations of BPA and benzophenones with reproductive hormones and semen quality appeared only in men with filaggrin skin-barrier mutations; parabens were not associated with any outcome.

references.authors: Jurewicz J, Radwan M, Wielgomas B, et al.
references.title: Human Semen Quality, Sperm DNA Damage, and the Level of Reproductive Hormones in Relation to Urinary Concentrations of Parabens.
references.finding: Urinary parabens were associated with more abnormal morphology, higher DNA stainability, lower motility and lower testosterone.

references.authors: Kiwitt-Cárdenas J, Arense-Gonzalo JJ, Adoamnei E, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of bisphenol A, parabens and benzophenone-type ultra violet light filters in relation to sperm DNA fragmentation in young men: A chemical mixtures approach.
references.finding: In mixture models, urinary 4-hydroxybenzophenone was associated with slightly lower sperm DNA fragmentation (about -5%); parabens, BPA and other filters were not associated.

references.authors: Li XT, Miao Y, Zhang M, et al.
references.title: Associations of paraben exposures measured by repeated urinary biomarkers with sperm DNA damage and apoptosis.
references.n: Chinese men from an infertility clinic, 2 urine samples each
references.finding: Butylparaben was associated with longer comet tail length and tail moment (sperm DNA damage), more so in overweight and younger men.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Yang T, Ye X, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of parabens and serum hormone levels, semen quality parameters, and sperm DNA damage.
references.finding: Methyl- and propylparaben were not associated with hormones, semen quality or sperm DNA damage; butylparaben categories tracked higher sperm DNA damage (p-trend 0.03).

references.authors: Nassan FL, Coull BA, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Personal Care Product Use in Men and Urinary Concentrations of Select Phthalate Metabolites and Parabens: Results from the Environment And Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study.
references.finding: Cologne/perfume and deodorant use raised urinary monoethyl phthalate by 83% and 74%; sunscreen and hand/body lotion raised urinary parabens by 66-156% and 79-147%, with the largest effects for use within 6 h of urine collection.

references.authors: Nassan FL, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Urinary triclosan concentrations and semen quality among men from a fertility clinic.
references.finding: Detectable urinary triclosan was associated with about 1 percentage point fewer morphologically normal sperm, without a dose-response, mainly before 2013 when exposure was higher.

references.authors: Nishihama Y, Toshima H, Yoshinaga J, et al.
references.title: Paraben exposure and semen quality of Japanese male partners of subfertile couples.
references.finding: No association between urinary parabens and semen volume, concentration or motility.

references.authors: Rehfeld A, Dissing S, Skakkebæk NE
references.title: Chemical UV Filters Mimic the Effect of Progesterone on Ca(2+) Signaling in Human Sperm Cells.
references.finding: 13 of 29 UV filters induced calcium signals in human sperm in vitro, nine by activating the CatSper channel like progesterone, some at nanomolar levels and additively in mixtures.

references.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
references.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
references.finding: In vitro, parabens raised mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS in human sperm and reduced motility and viability in a chain-length-dependent way; methylparaben at clinically used concentrations raised ROS and oxidative DNA adducts but not DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Shen X, Zhan M, Wang Y, et al.
references.title: Exposure to parabens and semen quality in reproductive-aged men.
references.finding: A paraben mixture was associated with lower sperm concentration, total count and progressive motility; butylparaben and methylparaben were the main contributors.

references.authors: Smith KW, Braun JM, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Predictors and variability of urinary paraben concentrations in men and women, including before and during pregnancy.
references.n: fertility-clinic men and women with repeated urine samples
references.finding: Intraclass correlations for methyl- and propylparaben were 0.42-0.54, so a single urine sample reasonably ranked exposure over several months; concentrations were 3.8 times higher in African American participants.

references.authors: Yuan G, Ma Y, Zeng Y, et al.
references.title: Associations between low-dose triclosan exposure and semen quality in a Chinese population.
references.finding: Low-level triclosan had limited (none or modest) associations with semen quality and was not associated with abnormal count or motility.

references.authors: Zhu W, Zhang H, Tong C, et al.
references.title: Environmental Exposure to Triclosan and Semen Quality.
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Triclosan was modestly associated with fewer forward-moving sperm and, in the lowest tertile, lower morphology, concentration and count.

references.authors: Zhu W, Xie C, Zhao S, et al.
references.title: Environmental Exposure to Triclosan and Male Fecundity: A Prospective Study in China.
references.finding: Higher male urinary triclosan was associated with lower fecundability (FOR 0.77) and higher infertility risk (OR 1.6).

references.authors: Braun JM, Smith KW, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Variability of urinary phthalate metabolite and bisphenol A concentrations before and during pregnancy
references.finding: During pregnancy ICCs were 0.50 for MEP, 0.45 for MBP, 0.25 for MBzP, 0.12 for BPA and 0.08 for sum-DEHP; one spot sample adequately classified MEP and MBP but not DEHP or BPA.

references.authors: Castellini C, Muselli M, Parisi A, et al.
references.title: Association between urinary bisphenol A concentrations and semen quality: A meta-analytic study
references.finding: Urinary BPA was only weakly associated with lower sperm motility, and the association disappeared after correction for publication bias; authors judge the link clinically negligible, if any.

references.authors: Dhar S, Tomar A, N A, et al.
references.title: Phthalates as the silent saboteurs of male fertility via changes in semen quality: a systematic review
references.finding: Systematic review without meta-analysis: MEHP, DEHP and DBP associated with lower sperm concentration and morphology; certainty of evidence low to moderate because studies are observational and heterogeneous.

references.authors: Dodge LE, Williams PL, Williams MA, et al.
references.title: Associations between paternal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations and reproductive outcomes among couples seeking fertility treatment
references.finding: Paternal MCPP and MCOP were associated with lower implantation and IVF live birth, but most paternal phthalate metabolites were not associated with outcomes.

references.authors: Duty SM, Singh NP, Silva MJ, et al.
references.title: The relationship between environmental exposures to phthalates and DNA damage in human sperm using the neutral comet assay
references.finding: An IQR rise in MEP was associated with 3.6 um greater Comet extent in sperm; other metabolites were not clearly associated.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Silano V, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Update of the risk assessment of di-butylphthalate (DBP), butyl-benzyl-phthalate (BBP), bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP), di-isononylphthalate (DINP) and di-isodecylphthalate (DIDP) for use in food contact materials
references.finding: EFSA set a group TDI of 50 ug/kg bw/day (as DEHP equivalents) for DBP, BBP, DEHP and DINP based on reduced fetal testosterone; aggregated dietary exposure was 0.9-7.2 (mean) to 1.6-11.7 (high) ug/kg/day, up to 23% of the group TDI; assessment called temporary.

references.authors: Génard-Walton M, Warembourg C, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Using mixture and exposome methods to assess the associations and interactions of chemical biomarkers with semen parameters
references.finding: Across four mixture/exposome models of 24 biomarkers (BPA, parabens, triclosan, 17 phthalate metabolites, hair mercury), the consistent signals were mercury (positive) and triclosan (negative); the overall mixture had small, imprecise associations with semen parameters.

references.authors: Ghayda RA, Williams PL, Chavarro JE, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol S concentrations: Potential predictors of and associations with semen quality parameters among men attending a fertility center
references.finding: Men with detectable BPS had lower sperm concentration (30.7 vs 38.3 million/mL) and semen volume, mostly among overweight men; BPS tracked fabric softener, paint and recent beef and cheese intake.

references.authors: Goldstone AE, Chen Z, Perry MJ, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A and semen quality, the LIFE Study
references.finding: In a general-population preconception cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with 34 of 35 semen measures; the only significant finding was less sperm DNA fragmentation with higher BPA.

references.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Duty S, et al.
references.title: Altered semen quality in relation to urinary concentrations of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
references.finding: Dose-response links of MBP with low sperm concentration (OR 3.3 top quartile) and motility; suggestive links for MBzP; single spot urine.

references.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Singh NP, et al.
references.title: DNA damage in human sperm is related to urinary levels of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
references.finding: MEP was associated with more neutral-Comet sperm DNA damage; MEHP was associated only after adjusting for the oxidative metabolite MEHHP (Comet extent +17.3%, tail % +17.5% per IQR).

references.authors: HELLER CG, CLERMONT Y
references.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration
references.finding: One cycle of the human seminiferous epithelium lasts about 16 days and complete spermatogenesis about 64 days.

references.authors: Johns LE, Cooper GS, Galizia A, et al.
references.title: Exposure assessment issues in epidemiology studies of phthalates
references.finding: Phthalate metabolite half-lives are 3-18 h; intraclass correlations of repeated urine samples are about 0.3-0.6 for DEP, DBP, DiBP and BBzP metabolites and 0.1-0.3 for DEHP, DiNP and DiDP; US and German exposures to DEP, BBzP, DBP and DEHP declined after 2001.

references.authors: Kiwitt-Cárdenas J, Adoamnei E, Arense-Gonzalo JJ, et al.
references.title: Associations between urinary concentrations of bisphenol A and sperm DNA fragmentation in young men
references.finding: No association between urinary BPA and sperm DNA fragmentation overall; a positive association only in the subgroup with SDF above 30%.

references.authors: Kortenkamp A, Martin O, Iacovidou E, et al.
references.title: Drivers of divergent assessments of bisphenol-A hazards to semen quality by various European agencies, regulators and scientists
references.finding: Analysis of why EFSA and the German BfR diverge: BfR proposed an alternative TDI 1,000-fold higher than EFSA's, based on adult sperm-count effects, and rejected the immunotoxicity endpoint; both agencies discounted gestational-exposure studies.

references.authors: Li DK, Zhou Z, Miao M, et al.
references.title: Urine bisphenol-A (BPA) level in relation to semen quality
references.n: 218 men with and without occupational BPA exposure (China)
references.finding: Men with detectable urinary BPA had more than three times the risk of low sperm concentration and vitality and more than four times the risk of low count; associations persisted at environmental levels.

references.authors: Liu C, Duan P, Chen YJ, et al.
references.title: Mediation of the relationship between phthalate exposure and semen quality by oxidative stress among 1034 reproductive-aged Chinese men
references.finding: Every phthalate metabolite rose with urinary 8-OHdG, 8-isoPGF2a and HNE-MA; 8-isoPGF2a suggestively mediated 12% of the MBP-sperm concentration link and 8-OHdG 32% of the MEP-morphology link (p<0.10).

references.authors: Lü L, Liu Y, Yang Y, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol A Exposure Interferes with Reproductive Hormones and Decreases Sperm Counts: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Studies
references.finding: Urinary BPA was associated with slightly lower sperm concentration and total count and with higher SHBG and estradiol, but not robustly with below-reference semen quality.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Ehrlich S, Toth TL, et al.
references.title: Semen quality and sperm DNA damage in relation to urinary bisphenol A among men from an infertility clinic
references.finding: An IQR rise in urinary BPA was linked to 23% lower sperm concentration, 13% lower normal morphology and 10% more Comet tail DNA.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Bellavia A, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Paternal mixtures of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A and parabens in relation to pregnancy outcomes among couples attending a fertility center
references.finding: A paternal DEHP-metabolite factor was linked to a higher probability of failing to reach live birth (HR 1.41 per IQR); the BPA/non-DEHP factor HR 1.24 (0.97-1.59) and parabens null.

references.authors: Radke EG, Braun JM, Meeker JD, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure and male reproductive outcomes: A systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
references.finding: EPA systematic review: robust evidence linking DEHP and DBP to male reproductive outcomes (AGD, semen, testosterone), moderate for DINP and BBP, slight for DIBP and DEP.

references.authors: Wang H, He H, Wei Y, et al.
references.title: Do phthalates and their metabolites cause poor semen quality? A systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies on risk of decline in sperm quality
references.finding: Urinary MBP (pooled OR 2.19) and MBzP (OR 1.88) and semen DEHP (r -0.23) were associated with low sperm concentration; no significant links with motility or morphology or for MEP and other metabolites.

references.authors: Akhigbe RE, Oyedokun PA, Akhigbe TM, et al.
references.title: Does pyrethroid exposure lower human semen quality? a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Pyrethroid exposure was associated with lower sperm motility, but results were inconsistent across regions (concentration lower in Poland, higher in the US) and all studies were cross-sectional.

references.authors: Anifandis G, Katsanaki K, Lagodonti G, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Glyphosate on Human Sperm Motility and Sperm DNA Fragmentation.
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: In vitro, glyphosate at 0.36 mg/L (far above environmental levels) reduced progressive sperm motility after 1 h but did not change sperm DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Chen YJ, Duan P, Meng TQ, et al.
references.title: Associations of blood trihalomethanes with semen quality among 1199 healthy Chinese men screened as potential sperm donors.
references.finding: Blood chloroform, brominated and total trihalomethanes were inversely associated with sperm count in cross-sectional and repeated-measure analyses.

references.authors: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Álvarez F, Arena M, et al.
references.title: Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance glyphosate.
references.finding: EFSA's 2023 peer review of glyphosate identified no critical areas of concern for human or animal health; it relied on ECHA's conclusion that glyphosate does not meet the criteria for classification as carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic, while listing data gaps (an impurity, consumer dietary risk, formulation co-formulants).

references.authors: Fenster L, Waller K, Windham G, et al.
references.title: Trihalomethane levels in home tap water and semen quality.
references.finding: Ingesting more than about two glasses a day of water with 80 ug/L THM was associated with 7.1 percentage points fewer normal-morphology sperm; authors noted limited exposure assessment.

references.authors: Giulioni C, Maurizi V, Scarcella S, et al.
references.title: Do environmental and occupational exposure to pyrethroids and organophosphates affect human semen parameters? Results of a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Organophosphate exposure was associated with lower ejaculate volume, sperm count and concentration; pyrethroid exposure was associated only with fewer normal-morphology sperm (WMD -7.6%).

references.authors: HELLER CG, CLERMONT Y
references.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration.
references.finding: Labelling of germ cells showed one seminiferous cycle lasts 16 days and the whole of human spermatogenesis takes approximately 64 days.

references.authors: Iszatt N, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Bennett J, et al.
references.title: Chlorination by-products in tap water and semen quality in England and Wales.
references.finding: In the largest study of public-water DBPs and semen, trihalomethane concentrations were not associated with poor semen quality (OR per 10 ug/L 1.01, 0.91-1.12).

references.authors: Ji G, Xia Y, Gu A, et al.
references.title: Effects of non-occupational environmental exposure to pyrethroids on semen quality and sperm DNA integrity in Chinese men.
references.finding: Urinary 3-PBA was inversely associated with sperm concentration and positively with sperm DNA fragmentation after adjustment.

references.authors: Lin X, Pan W, Liu J
references.title: Variability of urinary pyrethroid biomarkers in Chinese young-aged men and women over one year.
references.finding: 3-PBA reproducibility in spot urine was poor (ICC <0.15); at least four samples 3 months apart were needed for a reliable estimate over a year.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Barr DB, Hauser R
references.title: Human semen quality and sperm DNA damage in relation to urinary metabolites of pyrethroid insecticides.
references.finding: Urinary pyrethroid metabolites were associated with lower sperm concentration and motility and with more sperm DNA damage on the comet assay.

references.authors: Vasseur C, Serra L, El Balkhi S, et al.
references.title: Glyphosate presence in human sperm: First report and positive correlation with oxidative stress in an infertile French population.
references.finding: Glyphosate was detected in seminal plasma at about four times blood levels; seminal glyphosate tracked seminal 8-OHdG, and men with glyphosate had higher oxidant status and MDA.

references.authors: Wu WY, Wang DS, Lin HC, et al.
references.title: Urinary Glyphosate Concentrations and Serum Sex Hormones in a Nationally Representative U.S. Sample: NHANES 2017-2018.
references.finding: Higher urinary glyphosate was associated with lower AMH, androstenedione, oestrogens and progesterone and higher SHBG; the authors note the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

references.authors: Zeng Q, Li M, Xie SH, et al.
references.title: Baseline blood trihalomethanes, semen parameters and serum total testosterone: a cross-sectional study in China.
references.finding: Moderate blood bromodichloromethane and dibromochloromethane levels were associated with lower sperm count and linearity, with suggestive trends for concentration and testosterone.

references.authors: Zeng Q, Chen YZ, Xu L, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of exposure to trihalomethanes in tap water and semen quality: a prospective study in Wuhan, China.
references.finding: THM uptake via drinking water was associated with decreasing trends in sperm concentration and count.
